body: OK, will add a compat function, thanks

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**qualify hashlib.md5() with usedforsecurity=False** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4884
so that patch has the change which passes, however I cannot confirm for a FIPS python build.  if you have that available, feel free to test the above patch.

the lib says:
> Constructors for hash algorithms that are always present in this module are sha1(), sha224(), sha256(), sha384(), sha512(), sha3_224(), sha3_256(), sha3_384(), sha3_512(), shake_128(), shake_256(), blake2b(), and blake2s(). md5() is normally available as well, though it may be missing or blocked if you are using a rare “FIPS compliant” build of Python. These correspond to algorithms_guaranteed.

maybe an option is to switch to use (a substring of ) sha256 or similar?
the use of ~~sha1()~~ md5 is not for security purposes, why add the additional overhead ?

> so that patch has the change which passes, however I cannot confirm for a FIPS python build. if you have that available, feel free to test the above patch.

I need to figure out how to get the patched version into our build environment, but I am happy to confirm the fix once I do that.  (To confirm, this is not already available as a pip-installable branch of repo, correct?)

> the use of sha1() is not for security purposes, why add the additional overhead ?

it's actually faster on my machine
```py
import hashlib
import pathlib
import timeit

data = dict(
    tiny=b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit",
    small=b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.",
    large=pathlib.Path("README.rst").read_bytes(),
)
print({k: len(v) for k, v in data.items()})
print(hashlib.algorithms_available)

for alg in ["md5", "sha1", "sha256", "blake2b", "blake2s", "sha3_256"]:
    for k, v in data.items():
        print(
            alg, k, timeit.timeit(lambda: hashlib.new(alg, v).hexdigest(), number=100_000)
        )
```

we are actually using md5 tiny.
i guess md5 to me implies "this is not for security, at all", whereas the sha algos start looking like we are doing something for security.

Yes, I'm just suggesting alternatives if they start removing algos from python.
